external_collaboration.partner_name: University Prep Science and Math High School
external_collaboration.evidence_quote: At University Prep Science and Math High School in Detroit, engineering teacher Jack Pierick runs his Principles of Engineering and Conceptual Design classes the way real engineers work: start with a problem, prototype, test, and improve. Pierick's advice to teachers starting with PBL: expect things to go wrong, reflect after every class, and remember that reaching even one student makes it worthwhile.

PBLWorks has extensive experience with School Leader Networks through the Hawaii Innovative Leadership Network (HILN) and the Massachusetts SLN (MA SLN). These two successful PBLWorks PBL School Leader Networks have been thriving in Hawaii for 6 years and in Massachusetts for 3 years. Over this period, a total of 86 school leaders have engaged in these two SLNs, reaching over 182,000 students. Read more here about one what one of the HILN school leaders accomplished in their school.

We’re pleased to offer CEUs for our 3-day workshops, provided in partnership with Sonoma State University, a campus of the California State University system. Registration for CEUs will be available on the first day of the workshop until the last day of the workshop. CEU payments are non-refundable.

What PBLWorks has given University Prep Schools is not just a framework or a set of tools. They have transformed our teachers, our leaders, and our system in ways that will outlast any single school year or initiative.

network.stated_total_quote: Chronic absenteeism is complex, and there is no magic wand solution. However, it is meaningful that 20 of our 22 district partners saw a decrease in chronic absenteeism while working with us to implement Project Based Learning in their districts. The pattern is striking and consistent — 91% saw that kind of success, nor can it be random that 70% of those school districts saw greater decreases than their state average.
